title: v7.4 multi-session slowness: delegation mandate, silent-broken Jev hook, prose-triggered guard slow path
content: Measured 2026-10-14 (docs/analysis/multi-session-performance/). (1) The v7.4 'delegate every task, including small ones' rule makes 1–5-edit requests cost 65 vs 11 model calls and 12.9 vs 4.1 min (F-022); 3 of 7 v7.4 projects already override it by hand. (2) jev-gate.sh falls back to the global `rulebook` on PATH outside this repo; on the operator's machine that is a junction to F:\Node\hivellm\rulebook with no dist, so the prompt hook fails silently (~0.5 s per input, 8–16 s timeouts) in every project except this repo (F-007); it also fires on task notifications (75–94 % of runs) and renders 'ask the operator' whenever kind is null/unclear (gate.ts:584, F-040). (3) no-os-scheduling.sh matches keywords (' at ', 'batch', '.timer', scheduler names) against the whole payload incl. descriptions and file contents: 48 % of Writes take the slow path (+215–242 ms) and prose gets denied — it denied a heredoc writing this analysis (F-002). (4) Both guards print permissionDecision allow on every passing call = silent auto-approve of Bash/Edit/Write (F-039); replacing them with permissions.deny changes permission prompts. (5) npx @latest MCP launch = 4 processes, ~200 MB, ~1 s per session (F-013). (6) Codex never runs rulebook project hooks (untrusted) and reads AGENTS.override.md instead of AGENTS.md (F-033, F-034). Plan: 13 tasks phase1_*..phase4_v750-release on release/v7.5.0.
